od_031_position: OD-031 is PENDING. `Current Status`: 'Pending owner approval'. Its exact question is what triggers, authorizes and executes irreversible destruction when a `product_history`, `identity_commercial` or `security_audit` record reaches its 7-year retention maximum WITH NO accepted Account deletion or Organization closure request. Blocking Impact records: Volume II -- no, the retention-expiry path is absent rather than ambiguous; implementation -- no under `retention-destruction-trigger-interim-v1`; production -- no additional gate; feature -- every routine retention-expiry destruction behaviour and retention-cursor-driven partition drop are blocked until approval. The withheld limb is therefore exactly that: routine retention-expiry destruction with no tenant request. PERMITTED and contracted in full here: the LifecycleDeletionJob created by accepted Account deletion or Organization closure, which 016 STATE_MODEL.md names as its only entry condition, together with its manifest, modes, 30-day primary deadline, 35-day post-primary backup tombstone deadline, hold re-evaluation at every destructive checkpoint, retry, escalation, authorized replay generation and immutable Deletion Evidence. PROHIBITED and isolated under `retention-destruction-trigger-interim-v1`: no destruction, no job, no Deletion Evidence and no domain event when one of those three classes reaches its maximum without an accepted request; the record is retained in full subject to legal hold; the condition is recorded as Audit Evidence and operational telemetry under the existing `security_audit` and `operational_telemetry` classes, which need no event profile, and raises exactly one critical compliance escalation through the existing operational escalation path. Over-retention past a maximum is an approved, recorded, escalated, owner-visible compliance exception -- not a defect to be swept and not a domain event. No retention-expiry event may be minted: the Logical Event Envelope requires a producing `workflow_id`, an `event_profile` and a nonnull affected-entity triple, and no accepted profile admits a retention-cursor record with no aggregate. Concretely also prohibited: any retention-cursor-driven partition drop. schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md already presumes one and OD-031's Risks clause records that no higher layer authorizes it and that it must be corrected; this contract therefore does not implement it and does not treat the schema's presumption as authority. The limb is isolated on MTX-025, MTX-038 and MTX-093 only. Blocker: none -- OD-031 has no upstream blocker, only an absent owner decision.
od_031_scope_precision: OD-031's limb is bounded by class and by trigger, and MUST NOT be widened into ratified neighbours. MTX-038.request_schema: Per command, and always the Logical Command Envelope. Invitation create: Organization, normalized target email, canonical role, `permission_mode`, nullable persona, normalized scope, protected-permission preview, intended Assignment expiry, idempotency key, correlation ID. Invitation decide/revoke/reissue: opaque Invitation ID, expected state version, 20-2,000 character reason where required. Account suspend: Account ID, expected Account state version, nonblank 20-2,000 character reason. Account reactivate under `reactivation-proof-v1`: the ACTOR's current active Session with `mfa_satisfied=true`, `account.reactivate` in the target's Organization, expected Account state version, expected Organization authorization epoch, 20-2,000 character reason, and for a SecurityOperator one active Support Session naming the Account and exact action; it accepts NO Identity Validation Receipt. Account revoke/delete: Account ID, expected state version, reason. Organization suspend/reactivate: expected Organization state version AND expected authorization epoch, 20-2,000 character reason; reactivation additionally requires a fresh `organization_reactivation` receipt bound to the target Organization with `mfa_satisfied=true`. Closure request: expected versions, 20-2,000 character reason. Closure decide: Closure Request ID, expected state version, decision, reason. Legal Hold request/decide/release-request/release-decide: exact resource IDs and/or retention classes, inclusive UTC event-time interval, 20-2,000 character legal-purpose reason, expected state version. Support Session request/decide/revoke: Organization, resource and action allowlists, support-case or Incident ID, 20-2,000 character reason, expected state version. Deletion retry: failed LifecycleDeletionJob ID, expected state version, authorized new replay generation.
MTX-038.response_schema: The mutated record with its new state and incremented state version; for closure execution the closed Organization, its closed BillingEntity, the executed Closure Request and the created Organization LifecycleDeletionJob; for Account deletion the revoked Account and its LifecycleDeletionJob; for an accepted Invitation the Account, Role Assignment, Invitation and Session identifiers; for an approving release decision the released Legal Hold and each requeued blocked-deletion action. A denial returns its exact first-match reason with no record.

MTX-038.transaction_boundary: Account suspension: one transaction that atomically transitions active to suspended AND revokes Sessions before success returns. Account reactivation: one transaction validating the actor's own MFA-satisfied Session, both expected versions and the retained-grant set, restoring only still-active unexpired explicit Assignments. Organization suspension: one transaction changing active to suspended, recording the reason, incrementing both versions, revoking every active human Session and preventing new scheduled work. Closure request: one transaction creating the immutable Closure Request, which confers no state change. Closure execution: the single multi-root transaction in aggregate_boundary, allowed from active or suspended, rechecking expected versions, capturing the current legal-hold and retention snapshot and proving requester/approver separation. Deletion: immediate access revocation and logical deletion commit before success returns; physical and irreversible stages execute asynchronously and re-evaluate holds at EVERY destructive checkpoint. Completion is one transaction that persists the immutable Deletion Evidence and emits the completion event together, so no completion exists without its evidence. No external call sits inside a database transaction.
MTX-038.concurrency: The Organization authorization epoch is the serialization point for effective access, and it is a product requirement rather than a mechanism choice: Account suspend, revoke and delete and every Role Assignment revoke, reject, expiry and scope change that removes effective OrganizationAdmin authority serialize on it, so competing commands against DIFFERENT Accounts cannot both pass from the same epoch. The mutation is rejected as `last_organization_admin` unless another active Account already holds an active, in-scope, unexpired OrganizationAdmin Assignment or the same atomic transaction activates that replacement before removing the old authority. Closure: pending to approved/rejected/expired and approved to executed are the only transitions, so a decision racing the 24-hour due instant resolves with expiry winning at equality. Support Session and Invitation expiry likewise win at exact equality. Concurrent reactivation commands against one Organization commit exactly one transition; the loser observes the current state version and returns the stored result. A blocked expiry and a concurrent epoch advance serialize on the epoch, and exactly one `RoleExpiryBlockDecision` is written per `(role_assignment_id, authorization_epoch)`.
MTX-038.idempotency: Every command carries an idempotency key and its expected record state version; exact replay returns the stored result and commits no second transition, while an altered command under an existing idempotency identity returns `F1-DOMAIN-409 / idempotency_conflict`. Invitation creation is keyed by the open-invitation uniqueness preimage -- Organization, target-email digest, target identity when bound, canonical role, permission mode and persona, normalized scope, protected-permission preview and intended Assignment expiry -- with at most one pending-approval or active Invitation per full preimage; exact replay returns it and a different-key duplicate returns `invitation_duplicate_open` with the Invitation ID only while the requester remains authorized. Account deletion and Organization closure each create or replay exactly ONE LifecycleDeletionJob; exact replay duplicates no deletion. `RoleExpiryBlockDecision` is idempotent on `(role_assignment_id, authorization_epoch)`, so re-evaluating within an unchanged epoch writes no second decision and emits no second `RoleExpiryBlocked`. `DecideLegalHoldRelease` creates or replays each exact blocked-deletion due-now action once; there is no second release command.
MTX-038.background_job: Timed transitions run as ScheduledActions per BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md, each executed only by its named lifecycle service from the persisted deadline: `invitation_expire`, `role_assignment_expire`, `closure_request_expire` and `support_session_expire` on `control`; `organization_closure_execute`, `lifecycle_deletion_start` (within 60 seconds of acceptance), `lifecycle_deletion_attempt_due`, `lifecycle_deletion_deadline` and `backup_tombstone_verify` on `lifecycle`; `deletion_tombstone_invariant_sweep_due` on `maintenance`. Queue arrival time never decides a Volume I equality race; the receiving job rechecks the product deadline at transaction time. WITHHELD under OD-031: no retention-expiry sweep, cursor job or scheduled destruction action exists in this catalogue, and none may be added.
MTX-038.queue: `control` for expiry and authorization-epoch effects, `lifecycle` for closure execution, deletion manifests, key and object destruction and backup tombstones, `maintenance` for the deletion/hold/deadline/tombstone invariant sweep. Queue identity, ownership and per-process concurrency are owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row does not rename or re-topologise them.
MTX-038.retry_policy: Bounded and per-stage, exactly as `retention-interim-v1` fixes it: each primary, index, cache and key attempt has a 15-minute timeout and exactly ONE retry after 5 minutes, and only for `deletion_dependency_unavailable`. Schema, scope, digest, policy and authorization failures are nonretryable. A denied lifecycle command is terminal for that command and is never auto-retried. A failed job returns to queued only through an authorized new replay generation, never automatically.
MTX-038.terminal_failure: Closed Organization and BillingEntity, released or rejected Legal Hold, executed, rejected or expired Closure Request, accepted, declined, rejected, revoked or expired Invitation, revoked Account, and completed deletion job are terminal. Closed permits only retention and legal-hold job execution and immutable audit retrieval by authorized security or legal scope, and never reactivates. A missing or nonactive current BillingEntity returns `F1-DOMAIN-409 / billing_entity_state_invalid` and changes nothing; reserved `past_due` and `suspended` never exit through closure in the accepted baseline. Deadline failure or exhausted work emits `LifecycleDeletionFailed` and a critical escalation and NEVER fabricates completion evidence. All other transitions are invalid.
MTX-038.reconciliation: Blocked deletion remains blocked until exactly one hold release event queues it once against current policy; a changed policy may lengthen but never silently shorten an already accrued mandatory minimum. Failed replay requires a new authorized recovery generation; completed never reopens. Backup tombstones are written BEFORE primary completion and every restore applies them before any product read.
